A kilowatt-hour passes through factories and cities, revealing the pulse of industrial renewal. A microchip travels from laboratory to production line, recording the build-up and breakthroughs of innovation. A shipping container crosses ports and sea routes, charting an ever-wider world of trade. Each episode stands alone yet echoes the others. candidates.title: Crowds gather for ‘Lincoln at Gettysburg’ reenactment
candidates.excerpt: GETTYSBURG, Pa. — Hundreds of spectators were on hand Wednesday, Nov. 18, for the reenactment of President Lincoln’s arrival by train at the 1850s-era station in Gettysburg. The arrival of steam locomotive No. 17, an operational replica of a 4-4-0 supplied by the Northern Central Railway of York, via CSX’s former Western Maryland route, went according to plan. More than 18 months in the making, this carefully planned railroad operation involved coordination and close cooperation among a half-dozen stakeholders. It was part of Lincoln at Gettysburg: Shall Not Perish, a commemoration of Lincoln’s historic visit to Gettysburg 163 years ago and the celebrated address he delivered [see “America 250 event to reenact …,” Trains.com, Nov. 12, 2026]. Lincoln reenactor Billy Campbell was among numerous guests dressed in 1860s-era clothing, helping recreate the spirit and atmosphere of the time. candidates.title: Sea-Intelligence: NAWC Import Growth at 17.6% in September
candidates.excerpt: Following a sluggish start to the quarter, where laden imports contracted by ‑3.9% Y/Y in July and stabilized in August, September volumes surged to 1.45 million TEU. This double‑digit percentage growth in September is partially exaggerated by an unusually weak 2025‑Q3 baseline, when laden import growth dropped by ‑12.5 percentage points between July and September 2025. Still, 2026 marks the highest September laden import volume on record for the West Coast, eclipsing the previous high set in 2024. Overall, for 2026-Q3, NAWC ports recorded a 2.6% Y/Y increase in total container volume throughput, bringing the aggregate volume to 8.32 million TEU for the quarter. This growth was heavily weighted towards inbound cargo, with laden imports growing by 3.9% to reach 4.12 million TEU. In contrast, outbound cargo experienced more muted growth, as laden exports increased by just 1.8% to 1.21 million TEU, and empty container exports saw a smaller increase of 1.1% Y/Y to 2.67 million TEU. The vessel, MSC MARIANNA XVI, was named and delivered on 16 November, 135 days ahead of its contractual delivery date. candidates.title: Napier Port lifts earnings despite flat container volumes
candidates.excerpt: Napier Port reported further earnings growth for the financial year ended 30 September 2026, supported by a stronger cargo mix, higher container revenue and its yield-management strategy. Revenue increased by 11.7% to NZ$176.2 million, compared with NZ$157.7 million in the previous financial year. Reported net profit after tax rose by 15% to NZ$35.5 million. Underlying net profit increased by 30.5% to NZ$36.9 million. The port’s result from operating activities reached NZ$75.7 million, representing an increase of 17.9%. Its operating margin improved from 40.7% to 43%. “2026 was a strong year of service delivery and continued earnings growth for Napier Port,” said Blair O’Keeffe, Chair of Napier Port. “The result reflects the strength of our diverse cargo base, continued progress with our yield and cost management strategies, and the resilience of Hawke’s Bay’s primary sector,” he added. candidates.title: Who calls the shots when it comes to ship finance in Hong Kong?
candidates.excerpt: Who calls the shots when it comes to ship finance in Hong Kong? Tax incentives, Chinese leasing capital and a deep banking network are keeping Hong Kong relevant to global shipping. But the industry’s biggest question is whether deals are genuinely made in the city, or merely booked there. A major containership financing this autumn illustrates both Hong Kong’s reach and its limitations. Global Ship Lease’s new $1bn syndicated facility includes Bank of China (Hong Kong) and BOCOM Hong Kong among eight lenders supporting 15 newbuildings. But Bank of America is the bookrunner, and the money comes from a syndicate spanning three continents. A vessel can be ordered in China, owned through another jurisdiction, financed by multiple banks and leased to a charterer thousands of miles away. Where, then, does the financial centre sit? candidates.title: Stamford firms up 10 MR tankers in China
candidates.excerpt: Singapore-based Stamford Shipping has firmed up an order for 10 MR product tankers at China’s Nantong CIMC Sinopacific Offshore & Engineering (CIMC SOE), with the yard also securing two vessels of the same design from an unidentified European owner. The shipbuilder, part of Hong Kong-listed CIMC Enric, has confirmed that construction contracts covering all 12 ships are now effective, according to a Chinese shipbuilding industry report published on November 16. Each vessel will have a capacity of 49,900 dwt, giving the combined order a total of nearly 600,000 dwt. No contract value, construction timetable or delivery schedule has been disclosed. The deal marks the yard’s entry into the MR product tanker segment, adding a new vessel type to a portfolio dominated by LNG bunkering ships, LPG and ammonia carriers, and feeder containerships. candidates.title: Finom launches new credit products for SMEs in Germany and Netherlands
candidates.excerpt: Finom launches new credit products for SMEs in Germany and Netherlands European financial platform Finom has launched two new credit products for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Germany and the Netherlands, as it looks to address a gap in short-term business financing. The Amsterdam-based fintech business, which serves 300,000 businesses, has introduced a business overdraft and credit card, offering personalised limits of up to €20,000 (£16,700) and €40,000, respectively. The products use customers’ existing transaction data to make credit decisions in seconds, removing the need for businesses to submit annual accounts or bank statements. Finom said more than half of its customers now qualify for credit under the new offering, compared with between 11 per cent and 17 per cent under its previous credit product. candidates.excerpt: Two men were arrested after a shooting involving Union Pacific Railroad Police investigating suspected cargo theft near the busy Tehachapi Loop on Nov. 12. No injuries were reported, according to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office and reported in local media. The shooting occurred about 10:40 p.m. near Highway 58 and Broome Road, east of the loop. Railroad (NYSE: UNP) police were patrolling the area in response to recent thefts from trains when they discovered an open cargo-container door, authorities said. Officers began investigating, and a shooting occurred, according to the sheriff’s account. A suspect fled on foot, and railroad police secured the area and requested assistance from the sheriff’s office. Kern County detectives responded and took over the investigation. Investigators subsequently located Jesus Rodriguez, 32, in Keene and arrested him. candidates.title: Akiem Hicks
candidates.excerpt: Akiem Hicks was an interior defensive lineman for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who earned a 61.9 overall PFF defensive grade in the 2022 season, 60th among 127 qualified interior defensive linemans. His PFF pass-rush grade of 58.5 ranked 83rd among 127 qualified interior defensive linemans. His run-defense grade of 65.7 ranked 34th at the position. He generated 8 total pressures as a pass rusher. That total included 1 sacks, 4 hurries, 3 hits. Against the run, he recorded 15 solo tackles.
